title: Linear regression: closed form and gradient descent
hints: Prepend a column of ones to X so the intercept is just another weight: Xb = np.hstack([np.ones((N, 1)), X]). Then the model is Xb @ w and w[0] is the bias.
The closed form minimizes ||Xb w - y||^2. np.linalg.lstsq(Xb, y, rcond=None) solves it and stays finite when X^T X is singular; np.linalg.solve(Xb.T @ Xb, Xb.T @ y) only works when it is invertible.

For GD, the loss mean((Xb w - y)^2) has gradient (2 / N) * Xb.T @ (Xb @ w - y). Record the loss every iteration, then step w -= lr * grad. On standardized features lr = 0.1 converges in a few hundred steps.
